lines.text: Picked at random, outcomes equally likely → number of outcomes in the event $\div$ total number of outcomes; from a table or Venn diagram, divide by the grand total, outside region included ({{lesson:8.1}})
Probability something does not happen, or a missing value in a table of all outcomes → $1 -$ the probability that it happens, or $1 -$ the total of the others ({{lesson:8.1}})

Results of an experiment, or a probability that can't be worked out by looking → relative frequency $=$ times it happened $\div$ total trials; more trials usually give a better estimate ({{lesson:8.2}})
Is the dice, coin or spinner biased? → compare the relative frequency with the fair probability; a big gap after many trials suggests bias ({{lesson:8.2}})
How many times do you expect it → probability $\times$ number of trials; from a sample, use the sample's relative frequency as the probability ({{lesson:8.2}})
Two dice, two spinners or a coin and a spinner, all equally likely → sample space diagram: count the cells you want $\div$ all the cells, both orders counted ({{lesson:8.3}})
Two or more stages with given probabilities, or picks put back → tree diagram: multiply along each path, add the paths you want ({{lesson:8.3}})
At least one → $1 -$ the probability of none ({{lesson:8.3}})
Picks not put back (taken and eaten, without replacement) → tree diagram: on each later branch take $1$ off the total, and $1$ off the type already picked ({{lesson:8.3}})
$\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)$ or $\mathrm{P}(A \cup B)$ from a Venn diagram of numbers → overlap, or everything inside $A$ or $B$ with the overlap counted once, $\div$ the grand total ({{lesson:8.3}})
Given that, or chosen from a group, in a table or Venn diagram → divide by the given group's total only, not the grand total ({{lesson:8.4}})
Given the second outcome on a tree diagram → add the paths ending in that outcome for the bottom; the path that also fits is the top ({{lesson:8.4}})
